speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked	the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (a) whether the Ministry collates data on online retail sales for local and foreign e-commerce; (b) if so, what is the sales volume transacted by Singapore-based residents with foreign companies via e-commerce over the past three years; (c) how has this overseas e-commerce impacted on local businesses; and (d) what is the Ministry doing to help local e-commerce businesses to improve their sales.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: The Government tracks Internet transactions made with locally-issued credit and debit cards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: About 3% of total retail receipts in Singapore come from e-commerce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: While e-commerce presents competition to our local retailers, it also gives Singapore retailers the opportunity to expand their reach to the region and beyond.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: This is in line with the retail ITM vision for a vibrant retail industry comprising a mix of highly productive omni-channel retailers and local brand owners with global footprints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: The Government will assist local retailers to build digital capabilities and enable access to e-marketplaces under the Retail ITM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: As part of the SMEs Go Digital initiative launched at Budget 2017, SPRINGSingapore and IMDA have pre-qualified e-commerce solutions that can be readily adopted by SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: In collaboration with partners like Google, SPRINGSingapore also provides support to SMEs to strengthen their digital marketing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: IE Singapore also helps companies leverage e-commerce to unlock growth opportunities in overseas markets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: Besides support through the Market Readiness Assistance scheme and the Global Company Partnership scheme, IE Singapore connects companies to global, regional or niche e-marketplaces that are relevant to their internationalisation strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) are also important multipliers to accelerate e-commerce adoption among SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: For example, the Singapore Retailers Association (SRA), with the support of SPRINGSingapore and Workforce Singapore, is developing an SME e-Commerce Accelerator Programme to help retailers build integrated strategic plans for omni-channel implementation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: Besides TACs, we have also seen greater participation from the private sector in supporting our SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: The 99% SME movement is a national initiative led by SingTel, DBS and Mediacorp.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: Initiated in 2015, the effort makes e-commerce accessible to more companies through the set-up of an e-marketplace and offering training opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: The Government also helps members of the retail industry workforce adapt and upskill to keep up with developments in e-commerce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry))
text: To support this, SPRINGSingapore has worked with SkillsFuture Singapore to develop a skills framework for the retail sector incorporating e-commerce and digital marketing, which will be launched later this year.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But one of the reasons why I am asking this question is in relation to a report by Visa several weeks ago highlighting that online transactions in Singapore have actually more than doubled in the past five years.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And it accounts for about 25% of total spending on Visa cards in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In relation to what the Senior Minister of State mentioned just now about public entities' data in relation to online spending, I would just like to enquire, first, whether that data is actually public and if there is a longer time series  for analysts to access and to assess Singapore's private consumption, to assess also Singapore's Gross Domestic Product growth going forward.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One of the reasons why I ask is, at the moment, I think it is not readily available in public whereas, if you see in the US and China, it is readily available.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It could be because of various reasons, but I would like to hear the Senior Minister of State's response to that.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: On top of that,  how can e-commerce data be made more available to the public, going forward?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The data that I mentioned earlier is from MAS which tracks the  Internet transactions being made with locally issued credit cards and debit cards.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Having said that, I think that gives part of the picture because the entities being tracked who are parties to the transactions may not only be retailers.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It could be, for instance, payment for bills and so forth.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Having said that, we are also aware that there are various commercial studies being done by consultants on the state of e-commerce.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, I would like to refer the Member to the figure that I cited earlier, which is, that 3% of retail receipts in Singapore are from e-commerce.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, this suggests that there is room for e-commerce to increase as a proportion of total retail activity in Singapore.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamed, please keep your supplementary questions short.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The analysis that the Senior Minister of State gave is really about e-commerce retail sales in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But I think the crux of the question here would be: Singaporeans are spending more, but are they spending more internationally with international brand retailers compared to, say, local ones?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Are we losing out in terms of GDP for our local retailers to e-commerce?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Part of this would involve omni-channel capability building.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It also involves up-skilling the workforce so that our retailers will be able to draw on expertise who understand how to operate in an e-commerce environment.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But I think this also involves, generally speaking, profiling Singapore brands in a variety of retail sectors.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is, indeed, a very challenging area but it is certainly a challenge that we recognise and which we are preparing our retailers for.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Leon Perera, keep it short, very brief, because your supplementary questions are longer than your original questions.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, this is something we will constantly do.
